{{short description|French mathematician}}
'''Odile Zink-Favaron''' (born May 3, 1938){{r|born}} is a French mathematician known for her research in [[graph theory]], including work on [[well-covered graph]]s, [[factor-critical graph]]s, [[spectral graph theory]], [[Hamiltonian decomposition]], and [[dominating set]]s. She is retired from the [[Laboratory for Computer Science (University of Paris-Sud)|Laboratory for Computer Science]] (LRI) at the [[University of Paris-Sud]].{{r|lri}}

Favaron earned a doctorate at Paris-Sud University in 1986. Her dissertation, ''Stabilité, domination, irrédondance et autres paramètres de graphes'' [''[[Independent set (graph theory)|Independence]], [[dominating set|domination]], irredundance, and other [[Graph property|parameters of graphs]]''], was supervised by Jean-Claude Bermond.{{r|mg}}

==Personal life==
Her father was poet and professor {{ill|Georges Zink|fr}}. [[Michel Zink]] and [[Anne Zink]] are her siblings.{{r|zink}}
